# Stablecoin and Instability with Trump and Musk - The Friday Market Wrap!

First listed: 2025-06-06 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Stablecoin and Instability with Trump and Musk - The Friday Market Wrap!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY) - 2025-06-06
- [Substack: Stablecoin and Instability with Trump and Musk - The Friday Market Wrap!](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/stablecoin-and-instability-with-trump-2a7) - 2025-06-07

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman remains cautious despite the market rebound, arguing that unresolved trade negotiations can still produce a bad outcome. He expects more dedicated nuclear-power deals, explains the Wells Fargo asset cap, and discusses Bitcoin and stablecoins. He is less skeptical of Bitcoin than before but has not invested and doubts its behavior as a hedge.

The forecast of more nuclear arrangements is supported by later deals. His insistence on separating a stablecoin business from a speculative token is useful. Macro assurance that only a trade war could disrupt growth is too sweeping, and his apparent contradiction between jobs headlines confuses different comparison baselines.

<a id="youtube-gbgPlVuZOqY-c003"></a>
### 003. AI power requirements will lead to more long-term nuclear-energy agreements.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 3:19-4:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=199s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: Following the June 2025 Constellation agreement

Meta later announced additional nuclear arrangements with several suppliers. This resolves the direction of deal activity, not eventual plant delivery or investment returns.

Assessment test: Count later signed agreements separately from energized capacity.

- [Meta and Constellation nuclear PPA](https://investors.constellationenergy.com/news-releases/news-release-details/constellation-meta-sign-20-year-deal-clean-reliable-nuclear) (2025-06-03): The 20-year agreement begins in 2027 and supports continued operation of the Clinton plant; it is not a new operational reactor delivered in 2025.
- [Further nuclear agreements with Vistra, TerraPower and Oklo](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/01/meta-nuclear-energy-projects-power-american-ai-leadership/) (2026-01-09): Meta announced additional nuclear arrangements after the Constellation deal. Announced future capacity is not all operating generation.

<a id="youtube-gbgPlVuZOqY-c004"></a>
### 004. Wells Fargo asset growth was constrained for years and the Fed has now removed that cap.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 4:06-5:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=246s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The regulator confirms removal after remediation. Other enforcement conditions remained, so the action was not the end of all restrictions.

Assessment test: Read the specific order and remaining obligations.

- [Wells Fargo asset-growth restriction removed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/enforcement20250603a.htm) (2025-06-03): The Fed removed the asset-growth restriction after required remediation. Other provisions of the enforcement action remained in place.

<a id="youtube-gbgPlVuZOqY-c005"></a>
### 005. The asset cap constrained Wells Fargo deposit growth and left a large opportunity if it regained its old market share.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 5:11-5:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=311s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

An overall balance-sheet cap can constrain funding growth, but deposits can also replace other liabilities. The stated $600 billion opportunity is a counterfactual share calculation, not an achievable immediate growth forecast.

Assessment test: Reconstruct the deposit-share arithmetic and test capital, liquidity and loan-demand constraints.

- [Wells Fargo asset-growth restriction removed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/enforcement20250603a.htm) (2025-06-03): The Fed removed the asset-growth restriction after required remediation. Other provisions of the enforcement action remained in place.

### 008. Absent a trade war, the US economy will be fine.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 7:08-7:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=428s) | Stance: conditional | Horizon: not stated

Fine has no measurable threshold or horizon, and excluding one risk does not exclude other shocks.

<a id="youtube-gbgPlVuZOqY-c009"></a>
### 009. A moderating-jobs headline and a strong-data/rate-cut headline contradict each other.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 7:28-7:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=448s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A release can be weaker than the previous trend and stronger than the market expected at the same time. These are different baselines, so the headlines need not conflict.

Conditional reasoning: 139 is below 180 but above 100; moderation and an upside surprise can both be true.

Assessment test: Identify whether each comparison is against prior growth, consensus or a recession threshold.


<a id="youtube-gbgPlVuZOqY-c010"></a>
### 010. Current economic resilience can coexist with serious latent risks that markets temporarily dismiss.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 8:10-10:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=490s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The historical crisis record supports the distinction between delayed aggregate effects and deteriorating credit conditions. The analogy is not proof of an imminent new crisis.

Assessment test: Track leading credit indicators rather than relying only on current aggregate growth.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): The inquiry documents deteriorating mortgage vintages, weak underwriting, leverage, compensation incentives and institutional risk-management failures.

<a id="youtube-gbgPlVuZOqY-c012"></a>
### 012. Every EU country has a veto over the trade issues it cares about.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 11:26-11:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gbgPlVuZOqY&t=686s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Some matters require unanimity or national ratification, but qualified-majority voting is the general common-commercial-policy rule. The blanket veto explanation overstates the obstacle.

Assessment test: Identify whether a specific agreement is EU-only, mixed or in a unanimity category.

- [EU common commercial policy overview](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=LEGISSUM%3Aeu_trade_policy) (None): Qualified-majority voting is the general rule for EU trade agreements, with specified unanimity exceptions. This overview of the treaty framework was accessed November 10, 2026; it is not evidence of a 2026 rule change.

## Framework and tools

- A lack of immediate bad results does not eliminate latent risk.
- Follow physical infrastructure commitments behind AI enthusiasm.
- Understand regulatory constraints before extrapolating bank growth.
- Distinguish an asset narrative from observed return behavior.
- Separate a payment network from a token issuer business.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Nuclear power-purchase agreements
- Bank asset caps and deposit share
- Employment-data vintages
- Risk-asset correlations
- Stablecoin reserve income and remittance economics

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- Opening promotional snippets repeat later material.
- The May payroll number is the initial published estimate, not final revised data.
- The 2007 and First World War comparisons illustrate risk; he explicitly does not forecast a repeat financial crisis or a base-case trade war.
- Visa and Mastercard did not both go public in 2001; the chronology is incidental to the network-displacement thesis.
